unobservedGapBound.description: Memory contract v2 timer health for every memory-qualified take: no gap between two consecutive samples of the process's one memory series may exceed max(targetIntervalMultiple x the sampler cadence, floorMS), where a floor-tier take uses floorTiers.floorMS instead. The cadence is 250 ms on the 8 GB Mac, the iPhone and the 16 GB canonical M6 (the floor tiers sampled every 500 ms until 2026-09-25, when periodic ticks stopped enumerating threads) and 100 ms above, so the floor keeps one scheduler stall on a fast-cadence host from failing a take. Each take records the bound it met as samplerUnobservedGapLimitMS. Provisional: the first consented memory lane on the canonical M6 calibrates targetIntervalMultiple and floorMS, and a maintainer records that run here.

floorTiers.description: The floor tiers (the 8 GB Mac and the iPhone, by the device class each engine row stamps, forced or not) moved from a 500 ms to a 250 ms cadence on 2026-09-25, which would cut their bound from 1,000 ms to 500 ms while the only calibration data comes from the M6. They keep a 1,000 ms floor until a consented, unforced iPhone or 8 GB Mac memory-qualification record calibrates it (scripts/derive_memory_calibration.py --write on that record); an M6 calibration never moves it.

retainedMemoryV2.description: Reported beside retained-memory-v1 on the same run matrix. Each retained take publishes the MLX active and cache memory at its end (the snapshot after the routine post-generation cache clear, or after the stream on a tier that runs none) and the graphics-tagged footprint ledger at its end. Growth within a mode is the highest later retained take's MLX active memory minus the first's. It gates only once calibrated: until then every growthLimitMB is null and the record says uncalibrated.

calibration.requirement: One consented memory-qualification run per platform on its canonical host sets each mode's bound from that run's within-mode MLX growth noise; a maintainer records it here with the run ID.
